title: DMX-iGGA: 3 part lists in 3 rounds
summary: Join 72 synthesised parts into 13,824 distinct constructs in 3 rounds, over 6 protocols. Each round opens the library with BbsI, releases one part list with BsaI, ligates the two, and transforms, grows and preps the result for the round after it.

background.title: How this library is designed
body: One round appends one part list to every member of the library at once, so 3 rounds make 13,824 constructs out of 72 synthesised parts.
The product keeps BbsI's sites, which is what lets the next round open it, and loses BsaI's with the external stuffers.
Your vector already carried an internal stuffer, so every part enters position N on AGGA, which is the overhang that stuffer spells: DNA that exists cannot be re-chosen.
The overhang standard changes 27 amino acids across 26 part ends; changes.tsv has wild type beside synthesised, and that is what you are about to pay for.
The last round needs 195,386 colonies for a 0.99 chance that none of its 13,824 products is missing, which is 14x its products. A round short of that floor loses members no later round can put back.
The finished barcode block is 41 bp and reads in the reverse of the order the rounds ran; barcodes.tsv says which barcode names which part.

background.title: Read every well back
body: Both routes mark every well so that sequencing says which well a read came from, and both end with a pass or a fail for each well. Do one of them, never both.

How many wells each reaches is not what picks between them, and it does not rank them the way the bench's rule of thumb does. Barcode ligation addresses more than 330,000 wells from one plate of barcodes; index PCR addresses 9,216. Most runs sit well below either.

Barcode ligation carries a fixed cost and a fixed delay, paid once whatever the library's size: $695 of sequencing, and five days. Because they are paid once, the whole route costs less for each design the more designs there are, falling from $19.52 a design over 100 designs to $3.38 over 2,000. Nobody has published the same table for index PCR, so no price for it, and no price per well for either route, is stated anywhere here.

Index PCR runs one thermocycled reaction in every well, so thousands of wells need many thermocyclers. Barcode ligation needs none: a whole 1536-well plate marks in a single incubator. That is the only direct comparison of the two in print, and the barcode ligation route's own authors wrote it about the route they replaced; no independent measurement of one against the other was found.

Doing neither is also a choice. Every well is then enriched for the design it was built from, and nothing firmer than that can be said: the one published purity figure, 89.3% of 929 wells at 90% clonal purity or better, was measured on short arrayed fragments under 314 bases rather than on cargo from an oligo pool, and the same work found that polyclonality grows with length. Nothing measured says the material is even. To know what a well holds, read it back.

instructions: Order every row of pool.tsv as one synthesised oligo pool, 131 members at 350 nt.
notes: pool.tsv names each oligo's block, which piece of it that is, and the primers that pull it out, so an oligo is traceable to its protein.

troubleshooting.problem: The vendor bins the pool by length
troubleshooting.solution: Every oligo is padded to one length, so the spread is zero. A vendor asking for a different length wants this run's oligo length changed and the design run again.

steps.title: Resuspend the oligo pool
instructions: Divide the total yield in ng printed on the shipping tube label by 20, rounding down, to get the resuspension volume in µL.
Add that volume of 10 mM Tris buffer, pH 8.0 to the tube.
Vortex the tube until nothing is left undissolved.
cautions: Spin the tube down before taking the cap off.
notes: Dividing by 20 is what the vendor's own floor of at least 20 ng/µL comes to, and the amplification then pipettes 1 µL of 20 ng/µL: Twist Oligo Pools Amplification Protocol DOC-4060 REV 1.0, "Before You Begin".

steps.title: PCR1: pull 1 batch out of the pool
instructions: Set up 1 reaction, one a batch, with the pool as template.
Give each its own pair: batch 1: OP107 with OP146.
Run the program below. On a real-time instrument, add an intercalating dye and stop before the curve plateaus; the printed count is what to run without one.
notes: Every pair anneals at 65.1 °C, so one block of tubes takes them all.

Twist's band for a 350 nt pool is 12 to 14 cycles; Twist Oligo Pools Amplification Protocol DOC-4060 REV 1.0 gives the same three bands. Its FAQ answers that more cycles give worse uniformity, so 12 is what prints.
The outer primer is what makes a batch a batch: it is dropped at PCR2, so a block cannot be pulled out of a batch it does not sit in.

Batch sizes: 1 holds 72.

troubleshooting.solution: Drop the annealing temperature by 3 °C and check the pool went in.

troubleshooting.problem: A hump after the peak on a Bioanalyzer or TapeStation trace
troubleshooting.solution: Heteroduplexes, which is what over-amplification leaves. Run it again with fewer cycles. What too many cycles cost is dropout, chimeras and polymerase error; pooling the blocks equimolar later restores the evenness but none of those.

Run the program below. Nobody published a cycle count for this reaction, so run it on a real-time instrument with an intercalating dye and stop before the curve plateaus.

A block is named by its well from here on, not by anything in the tube.

troubleshooting.solution: Heteroduplexes, which is what over-amplification leaves. Run it again with fewer cycles; the forward primer is the whole batch's, so over-cycling here also pulls a neighbour's product into the well.

steps.title: Assemble each cargo into its position's destination, from its 1 to 5 pieces
steps.section: Close each cargo into its vector
instructions: Open DMX-iGGA N (block-vector-1.dna), DMX-iGGA DBD (block-vector-2.dna) and DMX-iGGA C (block-vector-3.dna) with BbsI and SrfI, the digest a round opens the library with, and clean each up.
Set up one assembly a well, holding that block's own PCR2 pieces, the opened destination of the position that block fills, and nothing from another well.
Transform, plate on 50 µg/mL kanamycin, and pick one colony a block.
notes: BsmBI cuts each oligo back to its fragment, so the primer sites, the recognition sites and the padding all stay outside the cargo.
The table is sized at the most pieces any block takes, so one master mix covers the plate; a well with fewer pieces fills fewer of its DNA rows.
A part enters on its own position's entry overhang, so there is one destination a position. They are one vector differing in the 4 bases of that overhang; a block put in the wrong one cannot close.

tables.title: Golden Gate assembly, NEBridge kit E1602

figures.caption: The stuffer BbsI cuts out of DMX-iGGA N, which a cargo replaces. The cargo enters on the four bases its position spells here.

expected: 72 plasmids, one a block: its position's destination carrying that block's cargo, 83 to 1,099 bp of it.

Each cargo reads: the overhang its part enters on, its coding bases, the internal stuffer, its barcode, and the TTCC cloning scar. The external stuffers parts.tsv spells either side of it are the destination's own bases.

troubleshooting.solution: A piece was missing from the well. Check that well's PCR2 lane before assembling it again; the pieces of one block are not interchangeable.

troubleshooting.problem: Colonies carrying the destination with no cargo
troubleshooting.solution: The destination was not opened to completion. Run a little of its digest on a gel before setting the plate up again.

steps.title: Array 72 designs and grow
instructions: Spot each design from its archive plate as its own spot on a 25 cm BioAssay plate.
Grow overnight at 37 °C on 50 µg/mL kanamycin.
notes: This run reads back every design, which a floor of zero does: 72 designs. The rest stay polyclonal and are never read one design at a time.
The archive is untouched: this reads a copy of it.
expected: One spot a design, at about 2,500 colonies a plate, which is the density picking wants.

troubleshooting.solution: That design has no clone to read. Re-transform it from the archive before anyone re-synthesises it.

steps.title: Pick 4 colonies of each design
instructions: Pick 4 colonies a design into 60 µL low-salt LB with 50 µg/mL kanamycin, with the QPix XE Microbial Colony Picker.
Fill one quarter of each 384-well plate before starting the next.
Grow overnight at 37 °C.
notes: 4 colonies a design is Lund's anchor and the only measured one; four gave a clean copy of 343 of 458 genes.
1 fragment: 40 designs, 100.0% of picks clean
2 fragments: 16 designs, 100.0% of picks clean
3 fragments: 6 designs, 93.8% of picks clean
4 fragments: 9 designs, 89.2% of picks clean
5 fragments: 1 design, 84.6% of picks clean
A quarter at a time is what makes a part-filled plate give full plates downstream, and what keeps a mark off a plate that is mostly empty.
expected: 288 wells over 1 plate: 288 picked.
Every colony of one design sits on one plate.

troubleshooting.problem: A design in many fragments gives no clean colony
troubleshooting.solution: The chances above say which designs that is likeliest for. Pick more colonies of those designs before the plates are poured, not after.

steps.title: Compress the picked plates into 1 barcoding plate
instructions: Invert the picked plates for 30 minutes so the cells gather at the meniscus.
Move 2 µL of each well into the 1536-well plate.

transfers.title: Compress 1 picked plates into lysate 1
transfers.note: Invert the picked plates for 30 minutes first, so the cells gather at the meniscus

expected: 288 wells of lysate, 4 picked plates to one.

steps.title: Barcode each well in lysate
instructions: Add one barcode from each of the 4 kit groups to every well, by the address that well's position gives.
Make each well up to 3.5 µL with 0.5 µL barcodes, 0.5 µL water and 0.5 µL master mix.
Run the ligation, then pool.
notes: The address is worked out from where the well is, not looked up: three groups name the well and the fourth goes across the whole plate from a reservoir.
The kit's sequences are not shipped. Read them from the copy you hold.

figures.caption: What a picked well holds: its design in the cassette DMX-iGGA N carries. The kit chains its 4 barcodes on, AGGA through TTCC, reading on the strand the cargo reads on.

expected: One barcoded construct a well, carrying four barcodes chained head to tail.

steps.title: Pool and sequence
instructions: Pool every well and amplify the three primer pairs separately. 2 miniprep columns, because one saturates.
Sequence the pool.
notes: Two plates on one flow cell are told apart by construction, because one axis of the address is the plate.
expected: Reads for 288 wells, every well told from the rest by the marks it carries.

steps.title: Call every well
instructions: Demultiplex the reads by address, checking each address rather than trusting a file.
Call a consensus a well, then compare it with that well's design base for base.
Reformat, compacting out the wells that failed.
notes: A well read too thinly carries no verdict and is not a failure, so reformatting does not compact it out.
More than one consensus is mixed, and mixed fails.
A design with no passing well is picked again from the same archive spot before anyone re-synthesises it.
expected: A well read more than 150 times is called.
A pass matches across the whole designed region: both entry overhangs, the fragment, the stuffer and the barcode.

troubleshooting.problem: A well's call is the right protein and the wrong barcode
troubleshooting.solution: It fails. A barcode that no longer names its member cannot be put right by the linkage read later.

steps.title: Pool each part list
instructions: Clean up each assembly and measure each concentration.

Pool the members of each part list in equal picomoles, one tube a position: each member gives the position's total divided by its member count, which is unequal masses because the members differ in length.
Bring each pool to at least 22.3 ng/µL. The round's 50 µL digest leaves 45 µL for the DNA after its two 2.5 µL enzymes, and the whole total has to arrive in it.

Equal picomoles are unequal masses: a short member weighs less than a long one for the same number of molecules, and weighing them equally would not pool them equally.

DBD: 0.219 pmol a member is 39.2 ng of its shortest at 291 bp and 48.9 ng of its longest at 363 bp.
C: 0.193 pmol a member is 15.8 ng of its shortest at 133 bp and 125 ng of its longest at 1,048 bp.
expected: N: one tube, 24 members, at least 1,000 ng at 22.3 ng/µL or above, 0.11 pmol of each member.
DBD: one tube, 24 members, at least 1,000 ng at 22.3 ng/µL or above, 0.219 pmol of each member.
C: one tube, 24 members, at least 1,000 ng at 22.3 ng/µL or above, 0.193 pmol of each member.

instructions: Amplify the whole cargo out of the finished library, from the vector before the first AGGA to the vector past the final TTCC, so one read carries a member's parts and its barcode block together, on Linkage read forward and Linkage read reverse from library-read-primers.tsv, which give a 1197 bp amplicon.

Decode each read's block against barcodes.tsv, then read the coding bases beside it against the member that block names.
notes: The block reads in the reverse of the order the rounds ran: each round inserted its barcode ahead of the ones already there.
0.0% of the single-base deletions a barcode can carry leave a read another barcode of the same part list could leave, which no read can be assigned through.
This build passes the linkage read at 90.0% of reads carrying a barcode that still names its part. That is this run's own mark, not a published one.

The short amplicon is what makes repeating it cheap: linkage spans the whole cargo, this spans the block.

steps.title: Pick the working vector and confirm PaqCI opens it
instructions: Take one tube of pLVX-TetOne-dom stock.
Digest a little of it with PaqCI (R0745) and run it on a gel.
notes: PaqCI reads no site in any molecule sharing the final-assembly pot.
ccdB is what makes the assembly self-selecting: a vector that took no cargo keeps the cassette and kills its host.
expected: 10284 bp opens on AGGA and TTCC, giving up its 385 bp ccdB cassette.
Two bands and no more: PaqCI reads this vector nowhere else.

troubleshooting.solution: The cassette is not where the record says, or the enzyme has lost activity. Sequence the stock before assembling into it.

steps.title: Release the cargo with BsaI and PmeI
instructions: Digest the finished library with BsaI and PmeI at 37 °C.
Heat-kill, then leave the tube alone: nothing is purified between the two stages.
notes: One tube, two stages. Killing the releasing enzymes before the working vector goes in is what keeps them off its backbone.
expected: The whole 1076 bp cargo free, on AGGA and TTCC, out of 6435 bp of library.
PmeI cuts the backbone it came out of, so that backbone cannot close again.

troubleshooting.problem: The library backbone survives the assembly
troubleshooting.solution: The blunt enzyme missed, or the heat kill was short. Both show up as colonies carrying the round's own vector rather than the working one.

steps.title: Assemble the cargo into pLVX-TetOne-dom with PaqCI
instructions: Add 75 ng of working vector, PaqCI (R0745) and T7 DNA Ligase in StickTogether DNA Ligase Buffer to the release tube.
Run the cycling below without purifying anything first.
notes: 6435 bp of library goes in and the cargo alone comes out: the backbone the rounds ran in is shredded and stays behind.
The cycling is NEB's longer single-insert program, which it gives for library preparation rather than for cloning one gene.
75 ng of vector, at 2:1 cargo to vector, is what this run measured, not a published figure.

figures.caption: The end the library is freed on, which the working vector takes: BsaI leaves AGGA here.

expected: One circular final vector a member, about 10975 bp, joined on AGGA and TTCC.
The ccdB cassette is displaced, so a vector that took no cargo kills its host.

troubleshooting.solution: The working vector was not opened to completion. Check the pick step's gel before repeating.

steps.title: Clean the assembly up and electroporate into Endura ElectroCompetent Cells
instructions: Add SPRI paramagnetic beads at 1x the volume and elute in water, as every round did after its ligation.
Pulse at 1800 V, 600 Ω and 10 µF in a 1 mm cuvette.
Recover and grow at 30 °C, as every round did.
notes: This is a bottleneck like a round's, and the library can only lose members here. Electroporate all of the assembly rather than a measured part of it.
The settings are the cells' own and are keyed by their catalogue number, not set by this method.
ccdB does the selecting here, so the plates carry pLVX-TetOne-dom's own marker.
expected: At least 195,386 net colonies: the floor for the 0.99 chance this design asked for that none of its 13,824 distinct members is missing, equally represented.
At that count the chance a named member is missing is 7.27 × 10⁻⁷.
Near-empty plates from a no-cargo control beside it; what grows there is working vector that kept its ccdB cassette.

troubleshooting.problem: Fewer net colonies than the count above
troubleshooting.solution: The library has lost members in the transfer. Nothing downstream puts them back; repeat the assembly from more of the released cargo.

steps.title: Read representation in the final vector
instructions: Amplify across the barcode block again, on Final representation read forward and Final representation read reverse from library-read-primers.tsv, which give a 149 bp amplicon.
Sequence, decode each read against barcodes.tsv, and compare the counts with the read taken in the library backbone.
notes: Linkage is read once, in the library backbone; a barcode still names the same part after the move, because the move carries the whole cargo in one piece.

The forward anchor is the same retained internal stuffer, which travels with the cargo; the reverse anchor moved with the vector, so this pair is designed against the final record rather than reused from the read before the move.
expected: The same combinations, at a similar evenness. A combination seen before the move and not after it was lost in the transfer into pLVX-TetOne-dom.
At least 99.5% of what survived the move seen; a 90th/10th percentile skew ratio below 10, judged at 100 or more reads a member, which is 1,382,400 reads over 13,824 combinations.

troubleshooting.problem: Markedly fewer combinations than before the move
troubleshooting.solution: The transfer was the bottleneck, not the rounds. Compare the colony count with the step above before rebuilding anything.
